title: The National Movement 1885-1919: From Petitions to Mass Politics

questions.question: The Indian Association of 1876, one of the Congress's forebears, was founded in Calcutta by:
options: Surendranath Banerjea and Anand Mohan Bose
questions.rationale: Surendranath Banerjea and Anand Mohan Bose founded the Indian Association (1876); its Indian National Conference merged into the Congress in 1886.

questions.question: The first session of the Indian National Congress (1885) was held at:
questions.rationale: The Congress met at Gokuldas Tejpal College in Bombay on 28 December 1885, with 72 delegates and W. C. Bonnerjee as president; A. O. Hume was convener.

questions.question: The 'drain of wealth' theory, the Moderates' economic critique of colonial rule, was propounded in books by:
options: Dadabhai Naoroji and R. C. Dutt
questions.rationale: Naoroji's Poverty and Un-British Rule in India and R. C. Dutt's Economic History of India demonstrated how home charges and one-way exports kept India poor.

questions.question: The Swadeshi movement began in protest against:
questions.rationale: The 16 October 1905 partition of Bengal triggered boycott, national education, and song; it was annulled in 1911, the first big win of mass agitation.

questions.question: The Congress split between Moderates and Extremists took place at:
questions.rationale: The Surat Split of December 1907 broke the Congress over the presidential choice; reunion came with the Lucknow session of 1916.

questions.question: The Ghadar Party (1913) was founded in San Francisco by:
options: Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna
questions.rationale: Lala Har Dayal and Sohan Singh Bhakna founded the Ghadar Party in 1913 among Punjabi emigrants, planning a wartime rising after the Komagata Maru affair.

questions.question: Separate electorates for Muslims were introduced by:
options: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto reforms)
questions.rationale: Following the Simla deputation of 1906 led by the Aga Khan, the Morley-Minto reforms of 1909 legalised separate electorates — the constitutional seed of partition.

questions.question: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 is significant because:
options: It ended British rule in Bengal
Congress and the League agreed on a common reform scheme, with Congress accepting separate electorates
questions.rationale: At Lucknow in December 1916, Congress and the Muslim League presented joint demands, with Congress accepting separate electorates — the high point of cooperation, Jinnah bridging both.

questions.question: The Home Rule Leagues of 1916 were started by:
questions.rationale: Tilak founded his Home Rule League at Poona in April 1916, Annie Besant hers at Madras in September 1916, demanding self-government within the empire.

questions.question: The Rowlatt Act of March 1919 allowed:
options: Detention without trial, continuing wartime emergency powers
questions.rationale: The Rowlatt Act provided detention without trial; Gandhi's 6 April 1919 hartal against it opened the Gandhian mass phase, leading to Jallianwala Bagh.
